story_text.value:
I really love Solidworks. I hate how it crashes every 5 minutes when I do something a little too fast. I hate how I lose work by pressing Save. I hate how expensive it is, especially for 10-year-old bugs to still exist.

Thus, I built a FOSS Solidworks alternative in, you guessed it, Rust. It's still very early, but I'm aiming for full assemblies, feature trees, drawings, etc.

I really want it to replace Solidworks for me, and for you as well, so please, try it out, and see what you think. I'd greatly appreciate it.

Thanks!

story_text.value:
I have been a heavy YouTube user for years, mostly on the entertainment side. If I thought a section of a video was something I would want to watch later, bookmarking it somewhere via "Copy video URL at current time" was my only practical solution.

I created this extension so I can clip the video without leaving the page and rewatch it later, either on the video page or from the library that contains all clips.

I wanted the UI to feel completely native to YouTube's player. So the controls are appended to YouTube's own. While creating/editing a clip, a display-only clip range indicator appears over the seek bar, and YouTube's timestamp section is replaced with start and end anchors that are also displayed as timestamps, but with frame numbers.

The extension is available on GitHub and on the Chrome Web Store.

https://github.com/ferhatwi/carpe

title.value: Show HN: Carpe – Frame-accurate clip vault extension for YouTube

story_text.value:
A little while ago I built (vibed) a tiny Mac app to block websites via the hosts file. By default it imported some fairly popular adult filtering lists as well as social media etc.

It has been very effective; it would only take a few moments to switch off but it is enough of an interruption to often make me re-evaluate and proceed on.

I have a particular distain for current affairs and have found "the news" addictive for years, clearly at the detriment to my own mental health and sanity.

So, in a similar vein to the other lists I found, I have created a fairly comprehensive list of news sites that can be imported/used as you see fit.

To state the obvious, the absolute vast majority of the work was done via Claude and a small army of sub-agents.

title.value: Show HN: News Blocklist – a DNS blocklist of 14k news and current-affairs sites

story_text.value: EtherPK (https://app.etherpk.com) can now also work as a general purpose markdown editor. It can now open a folder that doesn't contain EtherPK graph and view and edit markdown, text and code files in place. We call it Plain Folder mode. In Plain Folder mode, EtherPK reverts to plain markdown for .md files (no wikilinks, tasks or indexing). However, many of the features that make EtherPK a great reading, and editing experience are still there, including a rich markdown viewer and editor, a PDF reading with annotations and EBook reading. Text and code files are supported also.

story_text.value:
Hi there :)

I've created this "skill that makes API skills" because of something that usually happens to me: start a new project, add libraries to it, and then agents I use don't know how to make the most of those libraries.

And that's usually because agents don't get much the APIs provided by the libraries, and then start making assumptions, working on a "figuring it out as we go" basis, which usually leads to messy code where intent is lost.

Usually, the documentation for an API is structured very similarly to a documents tree: an index (root), and a hierarchy of documents under it, most often not a very deep one.

Also, for complex skills, we have skill trees, where a root SKILL.md refers a hierarchy of other sub-skills under it, so agents can navigate the tree in order to find the right sub-skill for the task at hand.

Which gave me the following idea: take an API documents tree, its taxonomy too, and then derive a skill tree from those.

Do this for an API's docs set, and you'll get an equivalent skill tree for that API, ready to be navigated by agents, in order to find the right subset of functions, datatypes, etc. to be applied to the case at hand.

This is what iskillz does: it provides the knowledge and tooling for my agent to inspect the API docs for some library I use, produce a skill tree for it, and then add that new skill to the current project, so the same agent can make the best use of the library's API.

Repo: https://github.com/anteloc/iskillz

title.value: Show HN: Iskillz – Turn API docs into API-usage skills for your project
